title: The Lion at the Gate
summary: Night on King's Parade. The college gates are locked, the gutters run the wrong way, and something with a mane is pacing behind the stonework.

intro.line: On Peas Hill a chip van glows like a lantern. Beyond it, along King's Parade, every college gate has been shut and bolted from the inside.

steps.text: Ask Old Mother Gadd about the trouble on King's Parade

dialogue.line: You look done in, love. Have a chip. Absalom sent you? Course he did. Bells, bells, always bells with that man.
I've kept this van sixty years and I've never seen the Parade like it. Clockwork porters, wound up tight, turning folk away from their own front doors.
Corvin's work?
His key, his oil. And there's a big cat on the Parade. Don't laugh. Stone-grey, size of a dray-horse, walking the top of the King's wall.
Go and stop those porters before somebody gets wound into the works. I'll keep the fat hot.

steps.text: Stop the Clockwork Porters patrolling King's Parade

intro.line: Three porters in bowler hats of riveted brass march the cobbles in step, keys ticking in their backs. As one, they turn towards you.

dialogue.line: The last porter winds down mid-stride. Its key is new-cut, and still warm.
Then the gutters of King's Parade start to run uphill, away from the river, carrying something pale with them.

steps.text: Drive back the Cam Wraiths rising from the gutters

intro.line: Cam water heaves up through the drain grates and stands into hooded shapes. The Undertide has found its way under the Backs and up the Parade.

dialogue.line: The wraiths slop back into the gutters. Where they rose, three carved stones lie on the setts: crest-stones, knocked from the parapet of the King's wall.
Each is warm and faintly ringing. Something wants them back.

steps.text: Recover the first crest-stone at the south end of King's Parade

dialogue.line: A carved rose, its petals worn smooth by five hundred years of weather. It hums one low note.

steps.text: Recover the second crest-stone below the King's wall

dialogue.line: A portcullis in miniature, chains and all. As you lift it, a growl rolls along the wall-top above you, too deep to be a dog.

steps.text: Recover the third crest-stone by Senate House Passage

intro.line: In Senate House Passage the walls whisper, in voices like old gravel. They are saying your name.

dialogue.line: Three stones: rose, portcullis, lily. Together they ring the note of the Gatehouse bell, and the gatehouse answers.
Back down the Parade, the carved lion above the King's gate is no longer there.

steps.text: Defeat the Gatehouse Lion before the King's gate

intro.line: It drops from the gatehouse in a slither of dust: a heraldic lion grown huge, crowned and shield-chested, guarding its hour-bell.
It roars, and the roar is the Gatehouse bell's note, struck far too hard.

dialogue.line: The lion shrinks into its stone again. You set the three crest-stones into the gate's carving, and the Gatehouse bell settles to a steady, sleepy hum.
Behind the gate the college lamps come on, one by one.

steps.text: Tell Old Mother Gadd the Parade is safe

dialogue.line: Heard it from here. Roared like a foghorn, then nothing. That's the Gatehouse bell steadied, that is. Three of twelve, love.
The porters were wound with a new key. Corvin's had keys cut for every lock on the Parade.
Then somebody cut them for him. And the water coming up the gutters, that's from the Backs. Something's opened a way under the river.
Here: a piece of the lion's shield. It took a hundred years of rain without a crack; it'll take a hit or two for you.
Now, that water. Folk up Bridge Street say there's a mist round the Round Church that won't shift. Follow the water, love, and you'll find who's letting it in.
